nodes.label: Maps app
nodes.summary: A user panning the map, asking for a route, and navigating with live ETA updates.

nodes.label: Tile CDN
nodes.summary: Caches tiles addressed by zoom, x and y; they change rarely, so they cache like static files.

nodes.label: Tile service
nodes.summary: Serves 256 x 256 pixel Web Mercator tiles at /zoom/x/y (or vector tiles); zoom n has 2^n x 2^n tiles, so most are rendered on demand.

nodes.label: Map data pipeline
nodes.summary: Builds the routable road graph and the tile sources from map data and publishes versioned artefacts. Our reference design.

nodes.label: Routing service
nodes.summary: Holds a preprocessed road graph in memory and answers route and distance-table queries (OSRM offers Route, Table, Match, Nearest, Trip and Tile).

nodes.label: Contraction hierarchy
nodes.summary: Nodes contracted in order of importance with shortcut edges; a query searches upward from both ends. About 0.2 ms per query on Western Europe in 2008, with negative space overhead.

nodes.label: Multi-level partition (MLD)
nodes.summary: OSRM's default: partition once, then a customise step applies new weights, which makes traffic updates cheaper than re-contracting.

nodes.label: GPS probes
nodes.summary: Anonymised location traces from phones and fleets. Their use as a traffic source here is our reference design.

nodes.label: Traffic pipeline
nodes.summary: Map-matches probes to road segments (OSRM's Match snaps noisy traces), aggregates current speeds per segment and keeps historical profiles. Pipeline shape is ours.

nodes.label: Segment speed store
nodes.summary: Real-time and historical speeds and travel times per segment; Google's ETA features use 17 two-minute live windows and 17-week time-of-day averages.

nodes.label: ETA model service
nodes.summary: Predicts travel time for a given route: a GNN per region over supersegments at fixed horizons, queried along the route with interpolation (Google Maps).

steps.caption: The app requests the tiles in view by zoom, x and y.
Tiles not in the CDN are rendered or read from the tile service and cached.

flows.name: Getting a route and its ETA

steps.caption: The app sends origin and destination.
The router searches the preprocessed graph with current weights and unpacks the path.
The chosen route is sent for an arrival-time estimate.
The model reads live and historical speeds and predicts each supersegment at the horizon when the driver will reach it.
Phones and fleets send anonymised location pings.
Pings are matched to segments and aggregated into current speeds.
The router's customise step applies the new weights and swaps them in.
Probe ingestion fails and current speeds go stale.
ETA falls back to historical speeds for this time of day and day of week, which the model already uses.
Routing weights stay at the last good values until the feed recovers; alert on staleness.

flows.name: A road closes before the map knows (failure)

steps.caption: Probes on the segment drop to zero flow.
The segment is given a closed weight in the next customise run.
Until then routes may still use it; navigating clients reroute when the next ETA update shows the delay.
